speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: Have you noticed any specific triggers or activities that worsen your neck and arm pain? Additionally, can you describe the pattern of your paresthesias—do they radiate in a specific way?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of diabetes and the progressive weakness in both hands, I need to determine if this is due to a cervical spine issue or diabetic amyotrophy. Does the pain worsen when you tilt your head to the side or extend your neck? Additionally, please tell me if you have noticed any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Peripheral Neuropathy (Diabetic)

The mention of a Urinary Tract Infection is incorrect and unrelated to your focal neurological deficits; we must rule out spinal cord compression immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST TEST: Nerve_Conduction_Study.
